title: Execution of All Suffix Instructions Staying in a Grid
summary: Given an n x n grid with a robot initially positioned at a specified start position and a string of movement instructions ('L', 'R', 'U', 'D'), determine the number of instructions the robot can execute starting from each possible instruction in the string.
statement: Given an n x n grid with a robot initially positioned at a specified start position and a string of movement instructions ('L', 'R', 'U', 'D'), determine the number of instructions the robot can execute starting from each possible instruction in the string. The robot stops if moving to the next instruction would exit the grid or if no more instructions remain.
constraints: The grid is n by n and start_pos is valid.
For each suffix s[i:], reset to start_pos and execute until the next move would leave the grid.
Return the number of successfully executed instructions for every suffix.
hints: Every suffix is an independent simulation from the same initial cell.
For each starting instruction, apply moves until the proposed next cell is out of bounds.
Reset row,column; increment count only after a valid move; append count when stopped or exhausted.
The loop follows precisely the suffix prefix that stays inside, so its count is the requested maximum executable length.
editorial: The loop follows precisely the suffix prefix that stays inside, so its count is the requested maximum executable length.

tests.explanation: The six suffixes permit 1,5,4,3,1,0 moves respectively.
Resetting for each suffix yields lengths four, one, zero, zero.
